title: When the Orchard Burns
premise: In 1919, in a border town where the armistice negotiations stall and revolution simmers, Paloma Voss works the punch-cutting bench in her late father's print shop, hiding her own talent behind his name. When a sealed letter arrives commissioning the shop to print forged armistice documents, the family is conscripted into a plot they never chose, and Paloma must decide whether to finish the work, sabotage it, or expose it. As soldiers close in and the orchard behind the shop burns, Paloma claims her father's craft as her own, cuts the decisive type by hand, and chooses love over inherited duty — signing the true armistice of her own life as the workshop falls.
about_author: Marguerite Pemberton is the pen name of a former typesetting apprentice turned archivist who spent a decade cataloguing private letters from postwar border towns. She writes from a converted bindery in the hills, where she still keeps her grandfather's gravers on the windowsill.

chapters.title: The Weight of a Letterform
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. We meet the print shop in its final quiet week: Paloma cutting punches in secret, her mother minding accounts, the town buzzing with rumors of the stalled armistice. She finishes a beautiful capital P in her father's style and signs his name to it. Beat: quiet longing — the ache of invisible excellence.

chapters.title: Sealed in Wax
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. A courier delivers a sealed letter commissioning the Voss shop to print documents 'of state importance' by month's end, with payment that could save the failing shop. Mother wants to refuse; the debt ledger says otherwise. Beat: dread disguised as opportunity.

chapters.title: The Apprentice Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Elias, a young soldier on leave and Paloma's childhood friend, arrives to deliver ink and lingers. Through alternating memories and present conversation, their unspoken love resurfaces — but he suspects the commission is forgery. Beat: warmth sharpened by suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Father Left
chapters.summary: Mother's POV. Searching the cellar for the old matrices, she finds her husband's hidden correspondence: he had printed for both sides for years. She realizes the commission is a debt being collected posthumously. Beat: grief curdling into fear.

chapters.title: Proofs in the Dark
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. Working nights, she begins setting the forged armistice text and discovers an error in the plate that would doom whoever uses it — deliberate or accidental, she can't tell. Elias warns that soldiers are asking about the shop. Beat: rising paranoia.

chapters.title: The Orchard at Night
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. Ordered to scout 'subversive printers,' Elias must choose between reporting the shop and destroying the evidence. He burns a cache of pamphlets in the orchard and is seen. Beat: love against duty, first fracture.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. An officer visits, polite and lethal, and Paloma must perform ignorance while her mother nearly breaks. He leaves a deadline: the work delivered in six days, or the family 'relocated.' Beat: terror under a civil mask.

chapters.title: Cutting the Truth
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV, the turning point. She decides to finish the job — but alters the documents so the forgery exposes its own falsity when examined. She cuts the decisive characters herself, signing her own mark for the first time. Beat: claiming identity through craft.

chapters.title: When the Orchard Burns
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The plot's conspirators discover the sabotage; soldiers torch the orchard and surround the shop. Elias defies his orders to shield the family; Mother confronts the officer with the father's letters as leverage. Beat: climax — fire, confession, and choice colliding.

chapters.title: The Last Impression
chapters.summary: Paloma's POV. The shop is lost, but Paloma pulls one final proof — her own name, her own face in type — and slips it into the armistice record before fleeing with Elias and her mother. The war ends not by their documents, but despite them. Beat: bittersweet resolution — inheritance reclaimed, love chosen, the past ash.
